British authorities say they have foiled
a suspected terror plot near an air base in western England.
It's one of the bases the US military has been using
to launch attacks on Iran that has fueled speculation
about a possible connection to the conflict
in the Middle East, NPR's Lauren Freya reports.
Police say it began with a middle-of-the-night phone call
reporting suspicious vehicles
near Royal Air Force Base Fairford.
They intercepted the vehicles and arrested five men
under both the Explosives Act
and the Terrorism Act.
President Trump praised the arrests, saying, quote,
"We had them under investigation.
"They were looking to do big damage."
Police have not identified the suspects,
nor said whether they were known to authorities
or under any surveillance.
Aerial footage shows a bomb disposal robot
maneuvering around three white vans on a tree-lined street.
About 85 households were evacuated.
Lauren Freya, NPR News, London.
The Department of Justice continues to defend
President Trump's decision to ban CNN, MS Now,
and Politico from the White House over their coverage
as court battles over media access
at the White House continue.
Speaking on ABC's This Week,
Attorney General Todd Blanche said it's not over.
The unfortunate and sad thing here
is that after years and years and years
of one-sided media coverage of the president
from certain outlets, the president finally said,
"It's not fair to the American people that this is happening
"and did something about it.
"There's still, obviously, litigation going on."
This weekend, CNN was blocked from Air Force One
for President Trump's visit to Tennessee.
Blanche declared the president has every right
to choose who flies with him.
A nor'easter this weekend brought strong winds,
high waves, and heavy rain to the island of Nantucket.
And yesterday, residents discovered ship remains
that may trace back to 1884.
NPR's Isabella Gomez Sarmiento reports.
Editor-in-chief of the Nantucket Current
was covering the storm when he received a tip
about wooden fragments from what appeared
to be a ship washed up on a beach.
Jason Graziadei went out to see the remains.
He told NPR they were in the same spot
as ship parts found in 2022.
At the time, researchers spent months
investigating the found wooden parts,
which resembled a ship's hull.
They concluded that the remains likely belonged
to the Warren Sawyer.
It was a Boston-bound cargo ship that crashed in 1884.
Although it's not certain yet whether the new remains
were once part of the Warren Sawyer,
Graziadei wrote to NPR that it's fascinating
to encounter a piece of Nantucket's maritime history.
Isabella Gomez Sarmiento, NPR News.
-A hurricane watch has been lifted for Hawaii's Big Island.
Officials are now taking stock of the storm's aftermath.
Several inches of rain fell across the Big Island yesterday,
which led to flooding on many roads.
This is NPR News in Washington.

says it has halted development of its latest models
shortly after disclosing its agents
scouring a federal government website,
acted in unexpected ways that suggested
they might have gone rogue.
This after AI evaluator Transloose
said that agents apparently from OpenAI
tried but failed to hack

OpenAI has not confirmed this.

at Katmai National Park and Preserve.

-As the brown bears continue fattening up on sockeye salmon,

they're all still winners.
-The bears have no idea that this is happening.
They have already won in the fact that they are set
to survive another winter hibernation.
-Voting in the bracket style competition
is closed over the weekend but reopens Monday.
Fat Bear Week ends Tuesday when a chubby champ will be crowned.
You can vote online at fatbearweek.org.
For NPR News, I'm Ava White in Anchorage.
-In a visit to Lourdes, France today,
Pope Leo XIV celebrated Mass
and spoke out against legislative efforts in France
and elsewhere to allow adults with incurable illnesses
to receive lethal medications.
He said those in extreme pain have an inherent dignity
that no law can eliminate.
I'm Louise Quivone, NPR News.
